findings.title: Reschedule calendar cleanup swallows getCalendar failures and reports success
findings.body: `getCalendar` used to be synchronous, so a throw from `new CalendarService(credential)` propagated out of this `forEach` and failed `requestReschedule`. The booking was already set to CANCELLED at line 475, but the reschedule email at line 570 had not been sent yet. The Google service constructor parses the stored key synchronously (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:31-38; the zod parse is at line 38), so a malformed key is one input that throws. Now the callback is `async`, so that rejection goes unhandled. There is no try around this block (the try at line 632 comes later). The mutation continues, sends the reschedule email, and returns success, while the old calendar event is not deleted and nothing reaches the user. The same applies to `deleteMeeting` at line 564. Suggested fix: resolve the calendar for each calendar reference with `await Promise.all(...)` before this `forEach`, so a `getCalendar` failure rejects the mutation as it did before. Keep the `deleteEvent` calls fire-and-forget as they were.
findings.originReason: getCalendar was synchronous in the base. This diff made it async and made the forEach callback async.

verification.reason: `getCalendar` is now async and does `await appStore[...]` before `new CalendarService(credential)`. Because the forEach callback at line 553 is async, a constructor throw (the Google zod parse at CalendarService.ts:38) becomes an unhandled rejection. The mutation then goes on to send the email at line 570 and returns normally. Before, the sync throw failed the mutation. The candidate's mention of a try at line 632 is wrong: that try is in the separate editLocation mutation, which doesn't affect the claim. Lowered to consider because deleteEvent failures were already fire-and-forget before this change, and the old behaviour also left the booking CANCELLED with no email sent.

findings.title: The try/catch around the calendar cleanup no longer catches anything
findings.body: The callback at line 125 is now `async`, so a rejection from `getCalendar` (line 128) no longer reaches the `catch` at line 135. Before, a synchronous throw from `new CalendarService` (for example the Google key parse, packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:38) was caught and logged with `logger.error` at line 137. Now it becomes an unhandled promise rejection that bypasses the logger. Suggested fix: resolve the calendar lookups with `await Promise.all(...)` inside the `try`, so their rejections are caught, and keep the `deleteEvent` calls fire-and-forget as before.
findings.originReason: The diff changed the callback to async and getCalendar to return a Promise.

verification.reason: The forEach callback at line 125 is now async and awaits getCalendar at line 128. Any throw, including the CalendarService constructor throw, now becomes a rejected promise that forEach drops, so the try/catch at lines 124-139 and its logger.error never see it. In the base, the sync getCalendar throw was caught and logged there.

findings.title: The try/catch around the calendar cleanup no longer catches anything
findings.body: Same change as in vital/lib/reschedule.ts. The `async` callback at line 125 moves the `getCalendar` rejection (line 128) outside the `try` at line 124. The `catch` at line 135 that logged `error.message` is now dead for calendar lookups, so a synchronous constructor throw becomes an unhandled rejection. Suggested fix: resolve the calendar lookups with `await Promise.all(...)` inside the `try`.
findings.originReason: The diff changed the callback to async and getCalendar to return a Promise.

verification.reason: Same pattern as vital: the async forEach callback at line 125 awaits getCalendar at line 128, so its rejections never reach the catch at line 135.

findings.title: Recurring-cancel calendar deletions are not awaited (pre-existing; the diff adds one more await)
findings.body: The outer `forEach(async ...)` is not awaited. Its pushes into `apiDeletes` happen after an `await getCalendar` (line 461) and after each `deleteEvent`. The next await-free stretch of the handler runs from line 622 to `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652, which snapshots `apiDeletes` before these callbacks push. So the calendar deletions for the other recurring instances are not awaited, their errors are unhandled, and the response returns without them. The `forEach` was already async before this diff, so this is pre-existing. The diff only adds one more await before the deletion starts. Consider collecting these promises and awaiting them, for example with `Promise.all` on the mapped array.
findings.originReason: The base already had the un-awaited `forEach(async ...)`, which pushed only after `await calendar?.deleteEvent`.

verification.reason: The async forEach at line 460 is never awaited, and every push into apiDeletes happens after an await. On the unpaid path there is no await between line 470 and the `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652, so those deletions are left out of the Promise.all. The base already had the same async forEach, with an awaited deleteEvent before each push.

findings.title: getCalendar promises are created before the variant filter drops some of them
findings.body: `getCalendar` is now async and is called at line 28 for every credential, before the `app.variant === "calendar"` check at line 29 discards some. Before, a synchronous throw here aborted the caller. Now a rejected promise that is discarded is an unhandled rejection. Is there a `_calendar` app whose variant is not "calendar"? If so, consider creating the promise only inside the variant check. I did not confirm whether such an app exists.
findings.originReason: getCalendar was synchronous in the base, so a throw propagated. The diff made it async.

verification.reason: Several apps have `_calendar`-suffixed types but a variant other than "calendar": hubspot, salesforce and sendgrid use "other_calendar", and closecom and zohocrm use "other". For those, the getCalendar promise created at line 28 is thrown away. Their constructors can throw synchronously; for example, closecom calls symmetricDecrypt. A throw there now becomes an unhandled rejection, where before it aborted the caller.

findings.title: The dynamic imports are eager, so no app is deferred until used
findings.body: `import()` inside the object literal runs when this module evaluates. So all 28 app modules start loading on the first import of `index.ts`, for example from packages/core/videoClient.ts:4. The change splits bundles and returns promises, but it does not defer any app until it is used. A module that fails to evaluate also becomes a rejected promise that stays unhandled until someone awaits that key. If per-app deferral is the goal, each entry would need to be a function such as `() => import("./x")`, and every `await appStore[...]` call site would have to call it. Is eager loading intended?
findings.originReason: The diff replaced the static `import * as` statements with eager `import()` expressions.

verification.reason: Each property value in the object literal is an `import()` call, and all of them run when packages/app-store/index.ts first evaluates (it is imported, for example, at packages/core/videoClient.ts:4). Every app module therefore starts loading right away; none waits until it is used. A module that fails to load gives a rejected promise that nobody awaits until its key is looked up.

findings.title: createMeeting: an import failure skips the Cal Video fallback
findings.body: `getVideoAdapters` is now awaited at line 52, before the `try` at line 70. If the selected app's module import rejects, `createMeeting` throws here, and the fallback to Cal Video in the `catch` at line 91 never runs. The lookup could not fail before this change. Consider moving the lookup inside the `try`, or confirm that an import failure should fail the booking instead of falling back.
findings.originReason: The diff made the adapter lookup await a dynamic import.

verification.reason: `await getVideoAdapters([credential])` at line 52 runs before the try at line 70. If the `await appStore[...]` import at line 26 rejects, createMeeting throws without reaching the Cal Video fallback in the catch at line 91. In the base, a failed module would have broken the whole static import of app-store instead, so this per-app failure path is new.

contracts.action: requestReschedule cancels the old booking, then cleans up its calendar and video references
contracts.before_after: Before: getCalendar was synchronous inside a forEach with no try around it, so a throw propagated out of requestReschedule. After: the callback is async and the rejection is unhandled. The email and success response proceed.
contracts.visible_effect: The mutation returns success and the reschedule email is sent, but the old calendar event is not deleted and no error is shown.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent. A malformed Google key (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:38) causes a failure that the user cannot see.

contracts.action: vital reschedule cleans up calendar and video references
contracts.before_after: Before: a synchronous getCalendar throw was caught and logged by logger.error. After: the async callback escapes the try, and the catch is dead for calendar lookups.
contracts.visible_effect: Nothing shown to the user. The error no longer goes through the logger.
contracts.failure_mode: Unhandled promise rejection instead of a logged error.

contracts.action: wipemycalother reschedule cleans up calendar and video references
contracts.before_after: Same as vital: the async callback at line 125 escapes the try at line 124.
contracts.failure_mode: Unhandled promise rejection instead of a logged error.

contracts.action: Recurring cancel: calendar deletions for the other instances
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:472 (single-booking path, pushed into apiDeletes and awaited at 652)
contracts.before_after: Before: the outer forEach was already async and not awaited (pre-existing). After: one more await (line 461) before the loop. The effect is the same: the deletions run after the snapshot at line 652.
contracts.visible_effect: The response returns before the other instances' calendar deletions finish. Their errors are unhandled.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent for deletions that fail. Calendar events for other instances can remain.

contracts.action: Old-booking cancel (no calendar credentialId): delete on every calendar credential
contracts.before_after: Before: forEach with a synchronous getCalendar and the deleteEvent promise pushed. After: a for-of loop with await getCalendar. The deleteEvent promise is still pushed to apiDeletes and awaited at line 652. The loop runs sequentially, which is slower but not different in outcome.
contracts.visible_effect: The same deletions, with a little more latency.
contracts.failure_mode: A getCalendar rejection throws out of the handler, as a synchronous throw did before.

contracts.action: Paid cancellation refund path resolves the payment app
contracts.before_after: Before: a synchronous lookup. After: await on the lookup. All four sites now await the same way.
contracts.visible_effect: None. The refund flow behaves the same.
contracts.failure_mode: An import rejection now throws from the await; previously the lookup could not fail.

contracts.action: connectedCalendars query and calendar availability API list calendars per account
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:94-111 (error entry for a failing calendar)
contracts.before_after: Before: getCalendar threw synchronously in getCalendarCredentials, outside any try, which failed the whole query. After: the rejection is held in item.calendar and awaited inside the per-calendar try in getConnectedCalendars (lines 46-48), so it becomes that account's error entry.
contracts.visible_effect: The failing account shows 'Could not get connected calendars'. The rest of the list still loads.
contracts.failure_mode: Visible per account, not for the whole list.

contracts.action: getCalendarCredentials creates a getCalendar promise for each credential
contracts.before_after: Before: the constructor ran synchronously for every credential, including those dropped by the variant check. After: the same happens, but as a promise that may be discarded.
contracts.failure_mode: A rejected discarded promise is an unhandled rejection, not a thrown error.
contracts.open_question: Can a credential whose app type ends in _calendar have an app variant other than 'calendar'? If so, its promise is discarded at line 29 without being awaited.

contracts.action: createEvent, updateEvent and deleteEvent in CalendarManager look up the calendar
contracts.before_after: Before: synchronous getCalendar. After: await getCalendar. deleteEvent is now async and returns the same Promise<unknown>.
contracts.failure_mode: Errors from the lookup now reject the returned promise, as a synchronous throw did before in the async functions.

contracts.action: EventManager merge path deletes the old calendar event
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/core/EventManager.ts:489 (the calendar deleteEvent call, already awaited)
contracts.before_after: Before: synchronous getCalendar followed by an awaited deleteEvent. After: await getCalendar followed by the same awaited deleteEvent.
contracts.failure_mode: The same as before, since this path is already in an async function.

contracts.action: getCachedResults and getBusyTimes fetch availability per credential
contracts.before_after: Before: map of synchronous getCalendar results. After: Promise.all over the same mapping. The index-based pairing with calendarCredentials is preserved.
contracts.failure_mode: A getCalendar rejection rejects getCachedResults, as a synchronous throw did before.

contracts.equivalent_path: packages/core/videoClient.ts:70-97 (the try block with the Cal Video fallback)
contracts.before_after: Before: a synchronous lookup, outside the try and without a failure path. After: await outside the try, so an import rejection escapes before the fallback.
contracts.visible_effect: The booking fails instead of falling back to Cal Video, but only when a video app's module import fails.
contracts.failure_mode: The error is thrown from createMeeting.

contracts.before_after: Before: a plain function; a synchronous throw from adapter.deleteMeeting threw directly. After: async, so the same throw becomes a rejection.
contracts.visible_effect: Callers that collect into Promise.all still fail as before. Callers that use fire-and-forget (bookings.tsx:564 and the reschedule files) now produce unhandled rejections.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent when the caller is fire-and-forget.

contracts.action: appStore is now a map of dynamic import() promises
contracts.before_after: Before: static imports, so every module was loaded when index.ts was imported. After: the same modules are imported eagerly through import() in the object literal, which runs at module evaluation time. Every consumer awaits the lookup.
contracts.visible_effect: None on the happy path. Bundles are split.
contracts.failure_mode: A module that fails to evaluate becomes a rejected promise that is unhandled until that key is first awaited.

contracts.action: getCalendar is async for every caller
contracts.before_after: Before: synchronous. After: async. The callers listed in the diff all await it, including handleNewBooking.ts:888 and the reschedule files.
contracts.failure_mode: Synchronous constructor throws now surface as rejections, which is the basis of the findings above.

summary: I read all 12 files in this part, plus their sibling call sites and the callers they reach. The main problem is the conversion of `getCalendar` to async. It has been applied inside `forEach(async ...)` callbacks in three places (bookings.tsx, vital and wipemycalother reschedule), which breaks the error handling those blocks had. In bookings.tsx a `getCalendar` throw used to fail the reschedule; now it is silent and the reschedule reports success. In vital and wipemycalother the try/catch is dead for these lookups. The other `await` conversions (payment lookups, `getConnectedCalendars`, `getVideoAdapters`, and the cancel paths) match their siblings. Also flagged: the new dynamic `import()` calls are eager, so no app is deferred. Nothing was built, tested or run; every claim comes from reading the code.
